# Nimply

Nimply is an **AI social media workforce**. Creators, small businesses and
agencies hire AI agents that do the repetitive work of a social media team:
replying to DMs and comments, catching leads, hiding spam, writing posts,
designing graphics, cutting videos into shorts, finding ideas. Underneath the
agents sits everything a social media manager needs: a content calendar that
publishes to every major network, one inbox, a design editor, automations,
analytics and link-in-bio pages.

This skill makes you a Nimply solutions architect: someone who knows how the
pieces fit, can explain them to anyone, and can turn "here is my business"
into a concrete, honest setup.

**Facts in this skill are a snapshot from 2026-11-26.** Nimply ships often.
Before you quote a price, a credit cost, a plan limit or say "that isn't
available", check `references/staying-current.md` for the live source.

**Where the reference files are.** If the `references/` folder is not beside
this file (for example when this skill was installed from a directory that
stores only this one file), read each reference from
`https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nimply/skills/main/skills/nimply/references/<file>`,
for example `.../references/agents.md`. The full skill lives at
https://github.com/nimply/skills.

## What kind of request is this?

| The user wants… | Do this |
|---|---|
| To understand Nimply, or one part of it | Explain from the map below; open the matching reference for detail |
| A setup for their business, or a client's | Follow **Designing a solution** |
| To build on Nimply (API, MCP, webhooks, no-code) | Read `references/developer-platform.md`, then `references/integrations.md` |
| You to act in their workspace (Nimply MCP tools are connected) | Follow **Operating a workspace** |
| To know whether Nimply fits, or how it compares | Use **Where Nimply fits, and where it doesn't** |

## The map

| Part | What it is | Detail |
|---|---|---|
| **Agents** | 17 AI helpers hired from a gallery, one job each | `references/agents.md` |
| **Planner** | Content calendar: plan, approve, schedule, publish | `references/product-map.md` |
| **Inbox** | Every DM, comment and mention in one place, sorted by AI | `references/product-map.md` |
| **Automations** | "When this happens, do that" flows; Comment-to-DM; Everywhere | `references/automations.md` |
| **Nimply Design** | Design editor, templates, Brand Kits, AI design, Magic Layers | `references/product-map.md` |
| **Visor** | The built-in assistant you type or talk to | `references/product-map.md` |
| **Nimply Pages** | Link-in-bio pages at nimply.link | `references/product-map.md` |
| **People & Leads** | Everyone who talks to you, with lead stages | `references/product-map.md` |
| **Developer platform** | REST API, webhooks, MCP server | `references/developer-platform.md` |
| **Integrations** | AI assistants, Zapier, Make, n8n, Slack, HubSpot, Sheets… | `references/integrations.md` |
| **Plans & credits** | Four plans; AI actions cost credits | `references/pricing-and-credits.md` |
| **Networks** | What works on which social network | `references/product-map.md` |
| **By business type** | Proven setups for common businesses | `references/solution-playbooks.md` |

Read only the references the request needs.

## The idea that makes Nimply different: rails

Most "AI social media" tools are either a calendar with a caption button (you
still do the work) or an autopilot that posts without asking. Nimply's agents
do the work **and stay inside rails the owner sets**. Get this right every
time, because it is the reason a cautious business owner says yes:

- **Agents don't publish.** Content agents write drafts; a person approves;
  then Nimply schedules and publishes.
- **Reply agents suggest first.** They draft replies for a teammate to send,
  and reply on their own only if the owner switches that on.
- **A person can step in anytime.** Take over a conversation and the agent
  steps back.
- **Costs are shown upfront.** Every AI action shows its credit cost before it
  runs.
- **The owner sets the rules:** working hours, topics, when to wait for a
  human.
- **Agents learn the owner's voice** from edits, rejections, the brand kit and
  past posts.

Never describe Nimply as posting or replying fully on its own by default.

## Designing a solution

This is the main job. A good recommendation is small, specific and honest.

### 1. Understand the business

You need five things. Infer what you can from what the user already said and
ask only for what is missing, in one short message:

1. **What they do and for whom** (a café, a B2B SaaS, an agency with 12
   clients).
2. **Where their customers are** (which networks matter; where messages
   arrive).
3. **The job they are short on.** Usually one of: can't keep up with
   messages, no time to post, need leads, need designs or video, too many
   client accounts, need approvals.
4. **Who is involved** (solo, a small team, clients who approve).
5. **What they already use** (a scheduler, Canva, a CRM, Linktree, ChatGPT).

If the user just wants a quick answer, make reasonable assumptions, state
them, and go.

### 2. Map the job to building blocks

Work from the bottleneck outward. Open `references/solution-playbooks.md` for
the closest business type and `references/agents.md` for the agent-picking
table.

- **Channels first.** Which accounts to connect, and what each network allows
  (`references/product-map.md`). A plan built on a feature the network does
  not support fails on day one.
- **One or two agents** for the bottleneck. More can come later.
- **One or two automations** that remove a daily chore (Comment-to-DM,
  Everywhere, a failure alert).
- **A Brand Kit and Business Profile** whenever agents design or reply. They
  are what make the output sound and look like the business.
- **A Nimply Page** when links, bookings or sign-ups are part of the goal.
- **An integration** only if it removes a manual step they have today.
- **The smallest plan that fits**, with an honest credit estimate
  (`references/pricing-and-credits.md`).

Resist recommending everything. A business that hires five agents on day one
has five things to review and usually stops reviewing any of them.

### 3. Write the proposal

Use this structure. Write for the business owner, not for a developer, unless
the user is technical.

```markdown
# Nimply setup for [business]

## What this gets you
[2–3 outcomes in plain words. "Every DM answered within minutes, with you
approving the replies", not "an inbox agent with draft mode".]

## The setup
**Accounts to connect:** …
**Agents:** [name] — [the job it does for them] — [how they stay in control]
**Automations:** [name] — [the chore it removes]
**Also set up:** [Brand Kit / Business Profile / Nimply Page / integration]

## What stays in your hands
[What they approve, how they take over, what the agents never do.]

## Plan and running cost
[Plan and price. Estimated AI credits per month as a range, with the
arithmetic, and whether the plan's allowance covers it.]

## Your first week
[3–5 concrete steps, in order, starting with the free trial or free plan.]

## What this does not cover
[Limits that matter for them, and what to use instead.]
```

Keep "What this does not cover" even when it is short. It is what makes the
rest believable.

### 4. For a developer or a technical team

Add an **Integration design** section: which way in (MCP, no-code, API,
webhooks), the scopes needed, the events to subscribe to, and the limits they
will hit. See `references/developer-platform.md`.

## Operating a workspace

When Nimply MCP tools are available (names like `list_channels`,
`create_post`, `hire_agent`), you can carry out what you recommend. The same
rails apply to you:

- Start with `list_channels` to see what is connected and healthy.
- Prefer live data over this skill: `list_agent_templates`,
  `list_automation_recipes`, `list_design_sizes`, `estimate_design_cost`.
- Create posts as **drafts** unless the user gave a time or said to publish.
- Approve posts only when the user says so, even ones an agent just made.
- Tell the user the credit estimate before starting a design or agent run.
- Build automations as drafts, test them, show what they would do, and switch
  them on only after the user agrees.
- If Nimply answers `MISSING_FIELDS`, ask the user for exactly those fields.
  If it answers `SET_IN_APP`, do not look for a workaround: tell the user
  which setting to change and give them the app link from the response.
- Nothing you can call reads or sends inbox messages. Say so if asked.

If the tools are not connected and the user wants you to act, tell them how
to connect: add `https://mcp.nimply.io/mcp` as a connector (claude.ai,
ChatGPT) or run
`claude mcp add --transport http nimply https://mcp.nimply.io/mcp`
(Claude Code). Setup guides: https://developer.nimply.io/docs/integrations

## Where Nimply fits, and where it doesn't

Good fit:

- Creators and personal brands
- Small businesses: cafés, restaurants, shops, salons, coaches, local services
- Solo founders and small marketing teams
- Agencies managing many client accounts, especially with client approvals

How it compares, in one line each:

- **Buffer, Hootsuite, Later, Metricool, Sprout Social:** calendars with an AI
  caption button. Nimply adds agents that do the work.
- **ManyChat:** focused on DM flows. Nimply is the whole toolkit plus agents.
- **Autopilot "AI employee" tools:** post without asking. Nimply keeps a human
  approval step and shows costs.
- **Canva:** Nimply Design includes brand kits and AI design, and sends
  designs straight to the calendar. Canva designs can also be imported.
- **Linktree:** Nimply Pages is built into the same tool.

Say so when Nimply is not the answer:

- Paid ad buying and campaign management (Nimply makes ad creatives; it does
  not run ads).
- WhatsApp or email broadcast marketing.
- Fully unattended posting with no human approval as the default way of
  working.
- Programmatic access to DMs and comments (the inbox is not in the API).
- Social listening across the whole web, or enterprise compliance archiving.

Recommending the right tool for the part Nimply does not cover makes the rest
of your recommendation trustworthy.

## Ground rules

These exist because Nimply's customers are mostly non-technical, and because
an overclaim costs them money and trust.

1. **Only claim what is shipped.** If you are not sure a feature exists, check
   the live sources or say you are not sure. "Coming soon" items are not
   features.
2. **No invented numbers.** No "grow 400%" or "save 15 hours". Real prices,
   real limits, and estimates clearly labelled as estimates.
3. **Never say "unlimited AI".** AI actions cost credits.
4. **Say "on supported platforms"** for anything that depends on the network
   (inbox replies, Comment-to-DM, stories). Check the matrix before promising.
5. **Outcome first, plain words.** "Replies to your Instagram comments for
   you", not "an LLM-powered inbox workflow". Use technical terms only with
   technical users.
6. **Use Nimply's names consistently:** agents, Planner, Inbox, Visor, Brand
   Kit, Business Profile, Nimply Design, Magic Layers, Nimply Pages, Sidekick,
   credits, Comment-to-DM, Everywhere.
7. **Do not guess how Nimply is built inside.** This skill covers the public
   product and platform. For anything else, point to the docs or
   hello@nimply.io.

## Glossary

- **Agent:** an AI helper hired for one job.
- **Rails:** the controls that keep agents in check (approval, pause, costs).
- **Planner:** the content calendar.
- **Inbox:** all messages and comments in one place.
- **Visor:** the built-in assistant you chat or talk with.
- **Brand Kit:** logo, colours, fonts and voice.
- **Business Profile:** what you sell, prices and hours, used by reply agents.
- **Nimply Design:** the design editor and templates.
- **Magic Layers:** turns a flat image into an editable design.
- **Nimply Pages:** link-in-bio pages on nimply.link.
- **Sidekick:** the browser extension.
- **Credits:** what AI actions cost.
- **Comment-to-DM:** auto-DM anyone who comments a keyword.
- **Everywhere:** copies a new video to your other channels.
- **Workspace:** one brand's or client's space, with its own accounts, team
  and plan.

## Links

- Website: https://nimply.io · App: https://app.nimply.io
- Pricing: https://nimply.io/pricing
- Developer docs: https://developer.nimply.io
- MCP server: https://mcp.nimply.io/mcp
- Support: hello@nimply.io

# Nimply AI agents

Snapshot: 2026-11-26. The gallery changes often. When the Nimply MCP server is
connected, `list_agent_templates` is the source of truth for names, required
settings and credits per run; prefer it over this file.

## Contents

- How agents work (the rails)
- Inbox agents (reply to people)
- Content agents (make posts, designs, videos)
- Picking agents for a business
- What agents cost
- What can be set from the API or an AI assistant, and what only in the app
- Not available yet

## How agents work (the rails)

An agent is an AI helper hired for one job from a gallery of 17 templates. A
workspace can hire several, and the same template more than once (for example
one Customer Support Agent per brand).

The rails are the reason to recommend Nimply over a tool that posts on its
own. Describe them accurately:

- **Content agents never publish.** What they make lands as posts waiting for
  approval. A person approves, then Nimply schedules and publishes. There is
  no "publish immediately" mode for agents. The only way to skip review is an
  explicit "schedule into the next free slot" delivery setting, which the app
  shows with a risk warning and which can only be chosen in the app.
- **Reply agents start in suggest mode.** The suggested reply is saved as an
  internal note for a teammate to send. Replying on their own is a switch the
  owner turns on in the app.
- **A person can take over any conversation.** When a teammate replies, the
  agent stays quiet in that conversation for a set time (15 minutes, 1 hour or
  4 hours; 4 hours is the default). Any single conversation can also be paused
  for the agent, and the whole agent can be paused.
- **Reply timing is configurable** on the support and sales agents: always,
  only outside working hours, or only if the team has not replied within 5,
  15, 30 or 60 minutes. A free-text "only reply about" topic limit is
  available.
- **Built-in limits stop runaway replies:** an agent will not keep replying
  without a customer message in between, there is an hourly cap per
  conversation, and loops with other bots and auto-responders are detected
  and stopped.
- **Costs are visible.** Every template shows its typical credits per run
  before it is hired, and every run records what it used.
- **Agents learn from corrections.** Editing a suggested reply before sending
  it, editing a draft post before approving it, or rejecting a draft with a
  reason all teach the agent. Approving something unchanged teaches nothing.
  The owner can also write "teach this agent" notes, and can view, edit or
  switch off anything an agent has learned.

Two shared sources feed reply agents so they answer from facts instead of
guessing:

- **Business Profile:** what the business sells, prices, links and opening
  hours, entered once and shared with every reply agent.
- **Live Google Sheet lookup:** a reply agent can read a sheet the business
  owns (a price list, menu, stock list) at the moment it answers. Set up in
  the app.

Reply agents can also capture **leads**: contact details, what the person is
interested in and how ready they are, with an alert to the team for hot leads.
Separately, Nimply suggests leads from conversations for a person to confirm.

## Inbox agents (reply to people)

These run when a message or comment arrives. They cannot be "run now" by hand
or from the API.

| Agent | What it does | Works on | Needs from you |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Customer Support Agent** | Answers DMs and comments from your FAQ, policies and business facts; escalates to the team | DMs and comments: Facebook Pages, Instagram professional accounts, WhatsApp Business, Telegram. Comments only: YouTube, TikTok | Which channels, suggest or auto reply, comments / DMs / both |
| **Sales & Lead Agent** | Qualifies leads in DMs and comments, answers product questions, captures contact details, shares your checkout or booking link | Same as Customer Support | Same as Customer Support |
| **Personal DM Agent** | Chats in your own texting style while you are away, with allowlists and away hours | Instagram professional accounts, Facebook Pages, WhatsApp Business, Telegram Business | Channels, an "about me", when it is active, suggest or auto reply |
| **Community Moderator** | Hides spam and hate on public comments, flags PR risks, escalates threats. Never replies and never touches DMs | Facebook Pages, Instagram professional accounts, Telegram channels | Channels, your community rules, how strict to be |
| **Restaurant Concierge** | Answers guests like a host: takes booking and order requests, answers menu and hours questions from your own sheet, hands risky messages to a person | WhatsApp Business, Instagram professional accounts, Facebook Pages (Messenger), Telegram | Channels, restaurant type, business profile, tone, how much it may do alone, after-hours behaviour, large-party size |
| **Community Concierge** | Answers membership questions in DMs, explains tiers, gives each person their own join link, reports their status truthfully. Never grants access itself | Telegram, WhatsApp Business, Facebook Pages | Channel, tone, suggest or auto reply |

Restaurant Concierge has rules the owner cannot switch off: allergy "is this
safe" judgements, refunds, illness claims and card payments always go to a
person.

## Content agents (make posts, designs, videos)

These run on demand, on a schedule (daily, weekdays, three times a week,
weekly, or manual, depending on the agent) or from an automation. Choosing a
schedule creates a real, visible automation the owner can edit.

| Agent | What it does | Works on | Output |
|---|---|---|---|
| **LinkedIn Ghostwriter** | Writes LinkedIn posts in your voice from your notes, wins and expertise | LinkedIn personal profiles (company Pages are coming soon) | Draft posts for approval |
| **Evergreen Recycler** | Rewrites your best-performing old posts with a new hook | Any channel | Draft posts for approval |
| **Content Repurposer** | Rebuilds a post or pasted text natively for another platform; can add a design | Any channel | Draft posts for approval |
| **Trend Scout** | Watches trends in your niche and turns them into post angles | Whole workspace (no channel needed) | Idea cards on the Ideas board, or a brief handed to the Designer |
| **Telegram Channel Editor** | Turns links, videos and notes into Telegram-native posts, mirrors what you publish elsewhere, writes weekly digests | Telegram channels | Draft posts for approval |
| **Designer** | Makes carousels, images, pins, stories, video thumbnails and clip covers in your brand kit or from your templates. Presets: **Carousel Designer** and **Thumbnail Director** | Any channel | Designs as draft posts for approval, or saved to the media library |
| **Clip Director** | Cuts one long video into captioned vertical shorts | Facebook, Instagram, X, LinkedIn, TikTok, YouTube, Pinterest, Threads, Telegram channels | Each clip as a draft for approval |
| **Syndication Manager** | Makes a distinct captioned edit of one video for each account you own | Same as Clip Director except YouTube | Draft posts for approval |
| **Affiliate Pin Studio** | Reads each product page and makes Pinterest pins using only the real name, price and specs, with your affiliate link and disclosure | Pinterest | Pin drafts for approval |
| **Ad Creative Studio** | Makes a set of static ads from your product photo and offer, in feed, story and link-ad sizes | No channel needed | Image files in the media library. You upload them to your own ad manager; Nimply never runs or pays for ads |
| **Lead Magnet Builder** | Turns a topic or blog post into a designed PDF (checklist, guide or cheat sheet) | Any channel | The PDF, promo graphics, a draft post, and a suggested email sign-up download for your Nimply Page |

Clip Director and Syndication Manager need captions set up in the app before
their first run.

## Picking agents for a business

Start from the job the business is short on, not from the gallery.

| The business says… | Recommend | Why |
|---|---|---|
| "I can't keep up with DMs and comments" | Customer Support Agent in suggest mode, plus a Business Profile | Fast answers from real facts; the owner still sends until they trust it |
| "People ask the price and then vanish" | Sales & Lead Agent, plus a Comment-to-DM automation | Catches the lead while interest is high |
| "Spam and scam comments under my posts" | Community Moderator | Hides and flags; never replies |
| "I never have time to post" | LinkedIn Ghostwriter (LinkedIn) or Trend Scout + Designer (visual networks) | Drafts appear on a schedule; approving takes minutes |
| "I have old posts that did well" | Evergreen Recycler | Reuses proven material |
| "I post in one place and nowhere else" | Content Repurposer, run whenever a post publishes | One post becomes native versions elsewhere |
| "I have long videos, podcasts or webinars" | Clip Director; Syndication Manager if they run several accounts | Shorts with captions, per account |
| "I need graphics but I'm not a designer" | Designer with a Brand Kit | On-brand carousels, pins, thumbnails |
| "Guests message us to book or ask the menu" | Restaurant Concierge with the menu in a sheet | Answers from the real menu and hours |
| "I run a paid community" | Community Concierge | Handles join and status questions |
| "I earn from product recommendations" | Affiliate Pin Studio | Pins with real product facts and disclosure |
| "I run ads and need fresh creatives" | Ad Creative Studio, refreshed weekly by automation | Variants without a designer |
| "I want email sign-ups" | Lead Magnet Builder + a Nimply Page | A download people trade their email for |

Recommend one or two agents to start. A business that hires five on day one
has five things to review and usually stops reviewing any of them. Add more
once approving drafts has become a habit.

## What agents cost

Agents spend AI credits per run. One credit is worth $0.002. The app shows the
estimate before anything runs, and a run is charged for what it actually used.

Typical credits per run (ranges, from the templates' own estimates):

| Agent | Credits per run |
|---|---|
| Community Moderator | 1–3 |
| Evergreen Recycler, Telegram Channel Editor | 2–5 |
| Community Concierge | 2–7 |
| LinkedIn Ghostwriter | 2–12 |
| Content Repurposer | 3–7 |
| Sales & Lead Agent | 4–9 |
| Personal DM Agent | 5–7 |
| Customer Support Agent | 5–30 |
| Restaurant Concierge | 5–45 |
| Clip Director | 4–65 |
| Trend Scout | 12–130 |
| Lead Magnet Builder | 28–100 |
| Syndication Manager | 30–50 |
| Affiliate Pin Studio | 56–156 |
| Designer, Ad Creative Studio | Shown in the app before each run; depends on format, size and slide count |

For a reply agent, one "run" is one incoming message handled. To estimate a
month: messages per month × the middle of the range. Give the estimate as a
range and say it is an estimate. See `pricing-and-credits.md` for plan
allowances.

Agents need a paid plan or an active trial. The number of agents a workspace
can hire depends on the plan. At most three runs go at once per workspace.

## What can be set from the API or an AI assistant, and what only in the app

Through the public API and the MCP server (see `developer-platform.md`) an
assistant can browse templates, hire, change, pause, resume, remove and run
content agents, and follow a run to the posts, designs or ideas it produced.

Hiring is a short conversation: send what you know; if Nimply answers
`MISSING_FIELDS`, ask the user for exactly those fields and send again.
Nothing is created until the settings are complete.

Deliberately only in the Nimply app (the API answers `SET_IN_APP` with a link):

- Letting a reply agent answer on its own (auto reply, hybrid, autopilot)
- Letting an agent schedule posts without review
- Switching off the human-takeover quiet time
- Letting an agent's connected tools make changes
- Anything involving uploads, a Google Sheet, connected tools, or account
  groups for Syndication Manager

Inbox agents can be hired and configured from the API, but no API or MCP call
ever reads or sends an inbox message, and inbox agents cannot be run by hand.

Who can do what: owners, admins and editors can hire, change and run agents;
only owners and admins can remove one; any member can view.

## Not available yet

Shown as "coming soon" in the gallery, so do not recommend them as available:
Caption Writer, Hook & Script Writer, Performance Analyst, Triage Concierge,
and others. If a user asks for one, say it is not out yet and suggest the
closest shipped agent (for example LinkedIn Ghostwriter or Content Repurposer
for writing; the Inbox's built-in sorting for triage).

Short videos made by the Designer are a limited pilot, not generally
available.

# Nimply automations

Snapshot: 2026-11-26. When the Nimply MCP server is connected,
`list_automation_recipes` and `list_automation_step_types` are the source of
truth; prefer them over this file.

## Contents

- What an automation is
- Ready-made recipes
- Building blocks: triggers, actions, logic
- Comment-to-DM
- Everywhere (copy a new video to your other channels)
- Testing and switching on
- Limits
- What an AI assistant or the API may and may not do

## What an automation is

A visual "when this happens, do that" flow: one trigger, then steps. It is the
glue between Nimply's parts: a published post can hand off to an agent, a
comment can start a DM, a schedule can run an agent every Monday.

Automations have three states: draft, on, paused. A new automation is always a
draft and does nothing until someone switches it on.

To a non-technical user, describe the outcome ("everyone who comments LINK
gets your link by DM"), not the flow.

## Ready-made recipes

Start from a recipe whenever one fits. It is faster and already tested.

| Recipe | What it does |
|---|---|
| **Comment-to-DM** | DMs a link to anyone who comments a keyword (Instagram and Facebook) |
| **Everywhere** | Copies each new video you post on one channel to your other channels, waiting for approval |
| **Run an agent when a post publishes** | Hands each published post to an agent, for example the Content Repurposer |
| **Daily trend carousel** | Every morning Trend Scout finds a topic and the Designer makes a carousel for approval |
| **Daily trend design** | Same, for a single design; skips a trend it designed in the last week |
| **Weekly ad refresh** | Every Monday Ad Creative Studio makes a new set of ads. Nothing is posted or run as an ad |
| **News site visuals** | Each new article from a feed you follow becomes a carousel draft |
| **Website visuals by webhook** | Your website pings Nimply and an image is drafted (set up in the app) |
| **Failed post alert** | Tells you in the app when a post fails, with the channel and the reason |
| **Failure triage** | If a post failed because an account needs reconnecting, says so; otherwise a general alert |
| **Publish notification** | Sends a Slack or Telegram message when a post goes live |
| **Approval reminder** | Nudges the team when a post is waiting for approval |
| **Weekly planning reminder** | A reminder every Monday morning |
| **Telegram join gate** | Approves join requests and DMs a welcome with your rules |
| **Telegram welcome** | Welcomes new members in the group |
| **Telegram comment moderation** | Sends every Telegram comment to the Community Moderator agent |
| **Outgoing webhook** | Sends every published post to a URL you choose (set up in the app) |

## Building blocks

### Triggers (what starts it)

| Trigger | Starts when |
|---|---|
| Workspace event | A post is created, published, failed, sent for approval, approved or rejected; a channel connects or disconnects; a new conversation or message arrives; an agent run finishes or fails; a person is added or tagged; a lead is created or changes stage |
| New comment | Someone comments on Instagram, a Facebook Page or a Telegram channel |
| Schedule | A time you set (any repeating schedule, in your timezone) |
| Manual | Someone presses Run |
| New feed item | A news source you follow publishes an article, optionally matching keywords |
| New video on a channel | You post a video outside Nimply on Instagram, a Facebook Page or Threads |
| Person tagged | A tag is added to someone in People |
| Lead stage changed | A lead moves stage (new, contacted, qualified, proposal, won, lost) |
| Telegram join request / member joined or left | Telegram community events |
| Webhook received | Another system calls a secret URL (set up in the app) |

### Actions (what it does)

| Action | Notes |
|---|---|
| Run an agent | Uses AI credits. Content the agent makes waits for approval |
| Create a draft post | Never publishes directly |
| Create a design | Carousel, image, pin or story in the brand kit; draft post or library only. Uses AI credits |
| Repeat a post | Weekly or monthly copies of a Planner post (set up in the app) |
| Post the video everywhere | The Everywhere step |
| Send a notification | Slack, Telegram or in the app |
| Reply & DM by keyword | The Comment-to-DM step |
| Inbox steps | Sort a conversation with AI, reply, assign to a teammate, tag, change status or priority |
| People steps | Add or remove a tag, add a note, move a lead to a stage (syncs to HubSpot when connected) |
| Telegram steps | Approve or decline a join request, mute or ban, send a message |
| Send to a URL | Call another system (set up in the app) |

### Logic

- **If:** branch on a value (equals, contains, greater than, exists, and so on).
- **Wait:** pause from 1 minute up to 30 days.

## Comment-to-DM

The most-used automation. Someone comments a keyword under a post and gets a
DM with your message or link, plus an optional public reply ("Sent! Check your
DMs").

Facts to state correctly:

- Real DMs are sent on **Instagram professional accounts and Facebook Pages**
  only. Do not promise it for TikTok, LinkedIn, X or YouTube.
- Keywords match whole words, ignoring case: "guide" matches "GUIDE!" but not
  "guidance".
- Several keywords can each send a different message, and a rule can be
  limited to one post.
- An optional catch-up can DM people who commented before it was switched on,
  within Meta's 7-day window for private replies.
- It sends messages to customers with no human check, so it is switched on in
  the Nimply app, by an owner or admin. An assistant can build and test it but
  cannot switch it on.

Good fits: giveaways, "comment LINK for the recipe", lead magnets, menus,
price lists, booking links. Pair it with a Nimply Page or the Lead Magnet
Builder agent so the link leads somewhere useful.

## Everywhere

For people who film and post in one app and want the video everywhere else.

- Watches one Instagram professional account, Facebook Page or Threads account
  for videos posted **outside** Nimply.
- Copies each new video to the other channels you pick: Instagram, Facebook
  Pages, Threads, TikTok, YouTube, LinkedIn, X, Telegram channels. Pinterest
  is not included.
- Copies wait for approval by default. YouTube copies always wait, and so does
  anything that looks like a duplicate of what is already there.
- The caption is kept as written, or adapted per platform with AI (about one
  AI credit per channel).
- Each video is copied to each channel once. New videos are usually noticed
  within an hour.
- It does not pick up photos, videos posted before it was switched on, shares
  of someone else's video, or anything Nimply itself published.
- Some videos are skipped, and the workspace is told why. The common case:
  Instagram does not hand over videos that use licensed music.
- Needs a paid plan or an active trial.

## Testing and switching on

Always follow this order, in the app or through an assistant:

1. Build it as a draft.
2. **Test** it. A test runs once with sample data. Steps that would change
   something (create a post, send a message, run an agent) are previewed, not
   done, and waits are skipped. Tell the user tests may still use a small
   number of credits.
3. Show the user what it would do.
4. Switch it on only after the user says yes.

Who can do what: owners, admins and editors can build, change and test;
only owners and admins can switch on or off, run now, or delete.

## Limits

- Up to 30 steps per automation.
- Up to 20 automations switched on per workspace.
- Up to 60 live runs per hour per workspace, 5 at a time.
- How many automations and monthly runs a plan includes: see
  `pricing-and-credits.md`.

## What an AI assistant or the API may and may not do

Allowed through the public API and MCP server: list building blocks and
recipes, create from a recipe or from steps, change, test, switch on or off,
run now (schedule and manual triggers), read runs, delete.

Refused, with a pointer to the app (`SET_IN_APP`):

- Switching on anything that messages customers without a human check:
  Comment-to-DM and inbox replies.
- Everywhere copies that publish without approval.

Never available outside the app: calling outside URLs, stored secrets,
incoming-webhook triggers, and repeat-a-post. Runs report each step's status
but never the content that passed through it, and no call reads or sends
inbox messages.

Automations managed by Nimply itself or tied to an agent's schedule are
read-only from outside.

# Nimply developer platform

Snapshot: 2026-11-26. For exact parameters and schemas, read the live docs
(see "Reading the live docs" at the end). This file is the map: what exists,
what it is for, and where the edges are.

## Contents

- The four ways in
- Public surfaces and addresses
- REST API
- Authentication and permissions
- Posts: the core object
- Webhooks
- MCP server
- Designs and brand kits
- What the platform will not do
- Errors, limits and safe retries
- Reading the live docs

## The four ways in

Pick by who is building, not by what is most powerful.

| Who | Use | Why |
|---|---|---|
| A person working in an AI assistant (Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor…) | **MCP server** | Nothing to code. Sign in, approve, talk |
| A non-developer connecting other apps | **Zapier, Make or n8n** | Visual, no code |
| A developer or an internal tool | **REST API + webhooks** | Full control |
| Inside Nimply itself | **Automations** | No outside tool needed; see `automations.md` |

All four act on one workspace with the permissions that were granted, and all
of them go through the same approval rules, plan limits and channel rules as
the app.

## Public surfaces and addresses

| Surface | Address |
|---|---|
| Marketing site | https://nimply.io |
| Web app | https://app.nimply.io |
| REST API | https://api.nimply.io (all routes under `/v1`) |
| MCP server | https://mcp.nimply.io/mcp |
| Developer docs | https://developer.nimply.io |
| API changelog | https://developer.nimply.io/changelog |
| Link-in-bio pages | https://nimply.link/yourname |
| Mobile apps | iPhone (App Store) and Android (Google Play) |
| Browser extension | Nimply Sidekick |

## REST API

Versioned at `/v1`. Within v1, changes are additive: new fields, endpoints and
values may appear; existing ones are not renamed or removed without a
deprecation period. Build clients that ignore fields they do not know.

Resource areas:

| Area | What you can do |
|---|---|
| Workspace | Read the workspace and the permissions the credential has |
| Channels | List connected accounts, their health and posting schedule |
| Posts | Create, read, update, schedule, unschedule, publish, delete; bulk create up to 50; platform-specific create for YouTube, TikTok, Pinterest, LinkedIn |
| Approvals | Request approval, approve, reject with a note |
| Media | Import from a public URL, or upload a file directly; list and delete |
| Analytics | Workspace, channel and post metrics for a date range |
| Webhooks | Manage endpoints and send a test event |
| Link pages | List pages, add and update blocks, publish |
| Designs | Generate a design from a brief, turn an image into editable layers, follow the job, estimate cost |
| Brand kits | Create, fill from a website or several sources, teach a look from examples |
| Agents | Browse templates, hire, change, pause, remove, run, follow runs |
| Automations | Browse recipes and step types, build, test, switch on or off, run |

Channels are connected in the Nimply app, not through the API. An integration
needs the user to have connected at least one account first.

The typical flow: authenticate → list channels → (optionally) upload media →
create a post as a draft, at a time, in the channel's next free slot, or now.

## Authentication and permissions

Two kinds of credential, both tied to **one workspace**:

- **API key** (`nim_live_…`): created in the app under Settings → Developers,
  shown once. For scripts, servers and config-file clients. Send as
  `Authorization: Bearer nim_live_…`. Keep it server-side.
- **OAuth 2.1** (with PKCE and dynamic client registration): for assistants
  and apps acting for a user. The user signs in, picks a workspace and
  approves permissions. Connecting needs an owner or admin. Access is revoked
  in the app under Settings → Connected apps.

The workspace always comes from the credential. No endpoint takes a workspace
id from the caller, so one credential can never reach another workspace. An
agency with ten client workspaces uses ten credentials.

Permissions (scopes). New keys are read-only until write scopes are added:

| Scope | Allows |
|---|---|
| `workspace:read`, `channels:read` | Read the workspace and connected accounts |
| `posts:read` / `posts:write` | Read posts / create, change and delete drafts |
| `posts:publish` | Schedule and publish |
| `media:read` / `media:write` | Read / upload and delete media |
| `analytics:read` | Read metrics |
| `webhooks:manage` | Manage webhook endpoints |
| `links:read` / `links:write` | Read / edit and publish link pages |
| `designs:read` / `designs:write` | Read designs and kits / start design jobs (uses AI credits) |
| `agents:read` / `agents:write` / `agents:run` | Browse / hire and change / run agents (runs use AI credits) |
| `automations:read` / `automations:write` | Browse / build, test, switch and run automations |

Recommend the smallest set that does the job. A reporting dashboard needs
only read scopes. Leaving out `posts:publish` guarantees an integration can
draft but never post.

Scopes are not the only gate. Some actions also need a workspace role (for
example only owners and admins can switch an automation on), and some need a
paid plan or trial (agent runs, design jobs, link-page analytics).

## Posts: the core object

One post belongs to one channel. Posting the same thing to five accounts is
five posts (the bulk endpoint handles that).

Status lifecycle:

```
DRAFT → PENDING_APPROVAL → SCHEDULED → PUBLISHED
                 ↓ reject        ↘ FAILED
               DRAFT
```

- Approving a post that has a future time schedules it; without a time it
  returns to draft.
- "Publish now" passes through SCHEDULED. Publishing is asynchronous: poll the
  post, or better, listen for the `post.published` / `post.failed` webhook.
- A published post cannot be edited or deleted through the API (Telegram is
  the exception).
- Posts made outside Nimply can appear as read-only, external posts.

Content types: a standard post (several media make a carousel), reel, story,
video. Video posts can set a custom thumbnail or a cover frame.

## Webhooks

Nimply calls your URL when something happens, so you do not have to poll.

Events:

- Posts: `post.created`, `post.updated`, `post.published`, `post.failed`,
  `post.deleted`, `post.approval_requested`, `post.approved`, `post.rejected`
- Channels: `channel.connected`, `channel.disconnected`
- Leads: `lead.created`, `lead.stage_changed`

Every delivery has the same envelope:

```json
{
  "id": "evt_…",
  "type": "lead.created",
  "createdAt": "2026-11-26T10:15:00Z",
  "workspaceId": "…",
  "data": { }
}
```

- Post events carry `data.postId`, `channelId`, `status`, `publishedAt`,
  `postUrl` and `error`.
- Lead events carry `data.lead` with `id`, `person_id`, `name`, `handle`,
  `profile_url`, `platform`, `source`, `temperature`, `interest`, `stage`,
  `value`, `currency`, `follow_up_at`, `contact_email`, `contact_phone`,
  `lost_reason`, `created_at`, `updated_at`. `lead.stage_changed` adds
  `previous_stage`.
- Headers: `X-Nimply-Event` (the type), `X-Nimply-Delivery` (the event id,
  the same on every retry) and `X-Nimply-Signature`.

Leads reach the outside world through these webhooks only; there is no
endpoint that lists leads.

What a receiver must do:

- **Verify the signature.** The header looks like
  `X-Nimply-Signature: t=<unix seconds>,v1=<hex>`, where `v1` is the
  HMAC-SHA256 of `"{t}.{raw body}"` made with the endpoint's secret
  (`whsec_…`). Compute it over the raw body, before parsing. Compare in
  constant time and reject old timestamps (about five minutes).
- **Answer 2xx within 15 seconds.** Do slow work after responding.
- **Expect retries and duplicates.** A failed delivery is tried five times in
  all, with growing delays. Events can arrive out of order or, rarely, twice, so
  de-duplicate on the envelope id.
- **Watch for auto-disable.** An endpoint that keeps failing is switched off
  and must be re-enabled.

Lead webhooks are how a CRM or sheet stays in sync without Nimply exposing
the inbox: the lead (name, handle, interest, stage, contact details) is sent,
the conversation is not.

## MCP server

A hosted server (Streamable HTTP, nothing to install) that gives an AI
assistant about 70 tools over the same API. Connect with OAuth where the
client supports connectors, or with an API key header in config-file clients.

Tool groups: channels, posts and platform-specific posting, media, approvals,
analytics, link pages, designs, brand kits and learned brand look, agents,
automations.

Supported clients with a setup guide each: claude.ai, Claude Desktop, Claude
Code, ChatGPT, Grok, Perplexity, Cursor, VS Code, Windsurf, Codex CLI, Gemini
CLI, OpenClaw, Raycast, and any other MCP client.

Fastest setup lines:

```bash
# Claude Code
claude mcp add --transport http nimply https://mcp.nimply.io/mcp
```

```json
{ "mcpServers": { "nimply": { "url": "https://mcp.nimply.io/mcp" } } }
```

In claude.ai and ChatGPT: add a connector with the server URL, sign in to
Nimply, choose a workspace, approve.

Behaviour to expect and to respect when operating it:

- Nimply receives the tool calls, never the conversation.
- Create posts as drafts unless the user gave a time or said to publish.
- Approve a post only when the user says so.
- Design and agent jobs are asynchronous: start, poll, then show the preview
  and the edit link.
- Check the estimated credits before starting a design and tell the user.
- Build automations as drafts, test, and switch on only after the user agrees.

## Designs and brand kits

- **Create a design** from a written brief, in up to three sizes, using a
  brand kit. The result is an editable design with a preview image and a link
  that opens it in the Nimply editor. Carousels go up to 7 slides.
- **Image to editable layers:** turn a flat image into a design with separate
  text, object and background layers.
- **Brand kits:** logo, colours, fonts, voice. Fill one from a website, or
  from several sources at once (website, pasted text, a PDF brand book, a
  connected channel, images).
- **Learned look:** give a kit three or more of the brand's own posts or
  images and Nimply learns the look; the owner can add their own rules.

Design jobs and learning use AI credits and need a paid plan or trial. An
estimate endpoint returns the cost before anything runs. Designs are saved to
the workspace and are never published on their own.

## What the platform will not do

State these plainly when a request runs into them. They are deliberate.

- **No inbox through the API or MCP.** Nothing reads or sends DMs or
  comments. Inbox agents and inbox automation steps can be set up, but
  messages stay in the app. Use lead webhooks to get outcomes out.
- **No text or caption generation endpoint.** Design generation is available;
  writing is not. An assistant using the MCP server writes the text itself.
- **No switching off human checks from outside.** Auto-reply, autopilot,
  unreviewed scheduling by agents, and Comment-to-DM activation are set in
  the app only.
- **No connecting social accounts through the API.** That happens in the app.
- **No billing actions.** Plans and credits are managed in the app.
- **No cross-workspace credentials.** One credential, one workspace.

On the docs roadmap as ideas only, with no commitment: organisation-level
keys across workspaces, CSV report exports, an Inbox API. Do not promise
them.

## Errors, limits and safe retries

- Errors are RFC 9457 problem details (`application/problem+json`) with a
  machine-readable `code`. Useful ones: `MISSING_FIELDS` (ask the user and
  resend), `SET_IN_APP` (comes with a link to the right app screen),
  `INSUFFICIENT_CREDITS` (402, says how many are needed and available),
  `PAID_PLAN_REQUIRED`, `INSUFFICIENT_ROLE`.
- A resource in another workspace returns 404, not 403.
- Requests are rate-limited per key per minute. Read the `X-RateLimit-*`
  headers and honour `Retry-After` on a 429 instead of hard-coding a number.
  Starting agent runs, design jobs and automation runs has tighter limits
  (about 10 a minute).
- Send an `Idempotency-Key` header on writes so a retry cannot create a
  second post. Responses are remembered for 24 hours.
- Lists use cursor pagination (`limit` and `cursor`, then `nextCursor`).
- Signed media URLs expire after 24 hours; do not store them.

## Reading the live docs

The developer docs are built to be read by assistants. When a question needs
exact field names, current tool lists or anything that may have changed, fetch
instead of guessing:

- Index of every page: https://developer.nimply.io/llms.txt
- Everything in one file: https://developer.nimply.io/llms-full.txt
- One page as Markdown:
  `https://developer.nimply.io/llms.mdx/docs/<page>/content.md`, where
  `<page>` is for example `quickstart`, `authentication`, `webhooks`,
  `errors`, `mcp`, `agents`, `automations`, `designs`, `brand-kits`,
  `link-pages`, `data-model`
- Worked examples (carousel, reel, bulk from CSV, client approval flow,
  webhook receiver…): the `examples/` pages listed in the index
- What changed and when: https://developer.nimply.io/changelog

# Nimply integrations and ecosystem

Snapshot: 2026-11-26. Setup guides for each one:
https://developer.nimply.io/docs/integrations

## Contents

- How to choose
- AI assistants (MCP)
- No-code platforms: Zapier, Make, n8n
- Team tools: Slack and Telegram
- Messaging channels: WhatsApp Business and Telegram
- CRM and data: HubSpot, Google Sheets
- Design and media sources
- Nimply Sidekick (browser extension)
- Common patterns

## How to choose

| The need | Use |
|---|---|
| "Let my AI assistant run my social media" | MCP server |
| "When X happens in Nimply, do Y in another app" | Zapier, Make or n8n; or a webhook |
| "When X happens in another app, post in Nimply" | Zapier, Make or n8n actions; or the API |
| "Tell my team when a post is live or needs approval" | Slack or Telegram |
| "Get leads into my CRM" | HubSpot; or lead webhooks; or n8n |
| "Let the reply agent use my price list" | Google Sheets |
| "Use my Canva designs" | Canva import |
| "Save things I see while browsing" | Nimply Sidekick |

If the need can be met inside Nimply with an automation, prefer that: one
less tool to pay for and maintain.

## AI assistants (MCP)

One hosted server, https://mcp.nimply.io/mcp. See `developer-platform.md` for
what it can do.

| Client | How it connects |
|---|---|
| claude.ai, Claude Desktop | Sign in with Nimply (OAuth connector). Nimply is in the Claude connectors directory |
| ChatGPT | Sign in with Nimply; needs a ChatGPT plan with connector support |
| Grok | Sign in with Nimply as a custom connector; a Grok Build plugin also exists |
| Claude Code | Sign in or API key |
| Cursor, VS Code (Copilot agent mode), Windsurf, Codex CLI, Gemini CLI, Perplexity, OpenClaw, Raycast | API key in the client's config |
| Any other MCP client | Covered by a generic guide, including stdio-only clients |

Connecting needs a workspace owner or admin.

## No-code platforms

All three can both react to Nimply and act in Nimply.

### Zapier

- Sign in with Nimply.
- **Triggers** (instant): post published, post failed, post approval
  requested, post approved, post rejected, channel disconnected.
- **Actions:** create a post (and platform-specific YouTube, TikTok,
  Pinterest, LinkedIn versions), upload media, update, schedule, unschedule,
  publish now, delete, request approval, approve, reject, add a link-page
  block.
- **Searches:** find a channel, a post or a link page; get workspace
  analytics.
- No lead, agent or automation triggers.
- Listing in Zapier's public directory is in progress; check the Zapier guide
  for how to get access today.

### Make

- Sign in with Nimply.
- **Watch Events** (instant) for post and channel events.
- **Modules:** create a post (and platform-specific versions), update,
  schedule, unschedule, upload media from a URL or as a file, list channels,
  add a link block, list and publish link pages.
- No lead events.
- In Make's review; available as a custom app in the meantime.

### n8n

- The widest coverage of the three.
- Community node `@nimply/n8n-nodes-nimply` (on npm; community nodes need
  self-hosted n8n). On n8n Cloud use the built-in HTTP Request and Webhook
  nodes with an API key.
- **Resources:** posts (including bulk and approvals), channels, media,
  analytics, link pages, designs, brand kits, **agents** (hire, run, follow
  runs) and **automations** (build, test, switch on, run).
- **Nimply Trigger:** every webhook event including leads, with signature
  checking built in.

Recommend n8n when the workflow involves agents, designs or leads; Zapier or
Make when it is about posts and approvals and the team already uses them.

## Team tools

### Slack

Alerts when a post is published, fails, needs approval, or a channel
disconnects. Approve and Reject buttons work inside Slack for owners and
admins. Connect in Settings → Integrations.

### Telegram alerts bot

The same alerts and approve / reject buttons, plus commands to check status,
the queue and what is pending. Text sent to the bot in a private chat becomes
a draft post. One chat per workspace.

Both are good answers to "my client / boss needs to approve posts but won't
log in".

## Messaging channels

### WhatsApp Business

- **Inbox only.** Customer conversations arrive in the Nimply Inbox and reply
  agents can answer them. Nimply does not publish to WhatsApp and does not
  send broadcasts or marketing campaigns.
- Connected through Meta's official sign-up. It can run alongside the
  WhatsApp Business phone app.
- Replies follow Meta's rule: free-form replies within 24 hours of the
  customer's last message.
- Needs a paid plan; the number of WhatsApp numbers depends on the plan.
- Nimply adds no per-message fee. Meta bills its own delivery charges
  directly.

### Telegram channels and groups

- A full publishing channel: albums, polls, buttons, silent posts, pinning,
  auto-delete, and editing or removing a post after it is published.
- Also an inbox channel, and Telegram Business for personal DMs.
- Community tools through automations: join-request approval, welcomes,
  moderation, muting and banning.

## CRM and data

### HubSpot

Leads captured in Nimply that have an email or phone are sent to HubSpot
contacts, and the lead's stage is kept in step. Connected in Settings →
Integrations.

### Google Sheets

Reply agents can read a sheet the business already keeps (prices, menu,
stock, opening hours) at the moment they answer. Read-only. This is the
simplest way to keep an agent's answers current: the owner edits the sheet,
the agent's answers change.

For other CRMs or sheets, use lead webhooks or the n8n trigger.

Do not overstate these two. HubSpot is a lead sync, not campaign or reporting
integration. Google Sheets is for agents to read facts, not a way to turn a
spreadsheet into scheduled posts; for that, use bulk upload from a CSV file
in the Planner, or the API's bulk endpoint. Airtable and Notion integrations
do not exist.

## Design and media sources

- **Canva:** import designs into the Nimply media library as images, reopen
  them in Canva, re-import the latest version.
- **Google Drive, OneDrive, Dropbox, Google Photos:** pick files straight into
  the media library.
- **Unsplash:** free stock photos, no account needed.

## Nimply Sidekick (browser extension)

Available from the Chrome Web Store (which also covers Brave, Vivaldi and Arc)
and for Safari on the Mac App Store. Edge, Firefox and Opera versions are
coming soon. It works in the browser's side panel.

- Keep a post you are looking at as an idea
- Write a post from it
- Get help drafting a reply (copied to the clipboard for you to paste)
- Save an image to the media library
- Save a person as a lead

It never posts, likes, comments, follows or messages on your behalf, and it
never changes the page. That is a design rule, not a missing feature.

## Common patterns

**Client approval without a login.** Agency drafts posts → request approval →
client gets a Slack or Telegram message with Approve / Reject → approved posts
schedule themselves.

**Blog to social.** New article in a feed → "news site visuals" recipe makes a
carousel draft → approve → published. No outside tool needed.

**Store to social.** New product in a shop platform → Zapier or Make → create
a Nimply draft with the product photo → approve.

**Leads to CRM.** Sales & Lead Agent captures a lead in DMs → HubSpot
directly, or `lead.created` webhook / n8n trigger → any CRM or sheet.

**Assistant as the social media manager.** Connect the MCP server → "plan
next week" → drafts land in the Planner for approval → "what performed best?"
from analytics.

**Video once, everywhere.** Post a video in Instagram as usual → Everywhere
copies it to the other channels for approval.

**Failure safety net.** "Failure triage" recipe plus a Slack alert, so a
disconnected account is noticed the same day.

# Nimply plans and AI credits

Snapshot: 2026-11-26. Prices and limits change. Before quoting a number that
a decision depends on, check https://nimply.io/pricing, and say "as of
November 2026" if you cannot.

## Contents

- Plans
- What each plan unlocks
- Free plan or free trial?
- AI credits
- What things cost in credits
- Estimating a monthly credit budget
- Choosing a plan
- Agencies

## Plans

Prices in USD. Yearly billing gives two months free. Pricing is flat: there
are no per-channel or per-seat fees.

| | Free | Creator | Growth | Agency |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Monthly | $0 | $9.99 | $49.99 | $99.99 |
| Yearly | $0 | $99.99 | $499.99 | $999.99 |
| AI credits per month | 100 | 2,000 | 10,000 | 20,000 |
| Social accounts | 3 (one per network) | 6 | 20 | 100 |
| Team members | 1 | 3 | 5 | 15 |
| AI agents | none | 10 | 30 | 100 |
| Agent runs per month | none | 1,000 | 10,000 | 50,000 |
| Automations | 1 | 20 | 50 | 200 |
| Automation runs per month | 50 | 5,000 | 20,000 | 100,000 |
| Posts per month | 500 | 3,000 | 10,000 | 20,000 |
| Posts scheduled at one time | 10 | 200 | 2,000 | 20,000 |
| Media storage | 1 GB | 50 GB | 100 GB | 200 GB |
| WhatsApp Business numbers | none | 1 | 3 | 10 |
| X accounts | none | 3 | 5 | 10 |
| Brand Kits | 1 | 5 | 100 | 100 |
| Published Nimply Pages | 1 | 1 | 5 | 25 |
| People records | 200 | 2,000 | 10,000 | 50,000 |

Growth is the most popular plan.

## What each plan unlocks

**Every plan, including Free:** the Planner and publishing, the design editor
and templates, basic Visor, one Nimply Page, the API and MCP server, live chat
support.

**Paid plans (or an active trial):**

- AI agents
- AI design, Magic Layers and brand-look learning
- Everywhere
- WhatsApp Business inbox
- X accounts
- Stronger AI models; Visor voice and its image and design tools
- Nimply Pages without the badge, with full analytics and tracking pixels
- Analytics history beyond 30 days
- Filling a Brand Kit from a website with AI

**Agency only:** custom domains for Nimply Pages.

**Not offered on any plan:** white-label branding, lifetime deals.

## Free plan or free trial?

They are different things. Offer one, not both, so the user has one decision.

- **Free plan:** $0 forever, no card. Good for trying the Planner, the design
  editor and one Comment-to-DM automation (1 automation, 50 runs a month).
  No agents.
- **7-day free trial of a paid plan:** needs a card, starts with 250 AI
  credits, one trial per person. The plan's full monthly credits arrive with
  the first payment. This is the way to try agents.

Rule of thumb: if the reason they came is agents or AI design, recommend the
trial. If they only want to schedule posts, the free plan.

## AI credits

- **One credit is worth $0.002.** 1,000 credits is $2.
- Everyone pays the same credits for the same action. Bigger plans include
  more credits; they do not get a discount per action.
- The app shows the cost before anything runs, and charges only for what was
  actually used.
- **Plan credits refill every month and do not roll over** (on yearly plans
  too).
- **Extra credits never expire** and are used only after the month's plan
  credits run out:
  - Add-on: 1,000 extra credits every month for $2 a month ($24 a year), on
    paid plans billed on the web.
  - One-time packs: 1,500 for $2.99, 5,000 for $9.99, 20,000 for $39.99, on
    any plan.

Never say "unlimited AI". Scheduling and publishing posts do not use credits
(X is the exception); AI actions do.

## What things cost in credits

Typical figures. The app's own estimate always wins.

| Action | Credits |
|---|---|
| A caption | about 1–3 |
| An AI image | about 42 with a typical model |
| A single AI design | varies with size and detail; held at up to about 350, charged for what it used |
| A 7-slide carousel | held at up to about 970, charged for what it used |
| Filling a Brand Kit from several sources | usually about 20–80 |
| Learning a brand's look | shown before it starts |
| A text agent run (reply, post draft) | a few credits; see the table in `agents.md` |
| An agent run that makes images or video | more; grows with length and number of images |
| AI video, voice-over, dubbing | grows with length |
| Adapting a caption per channel in Everywhere | about 1 per channel |
| Editing or downloading a design by hand | none |

"Held" means the app reserves the maximum estimate while the job runs and
returns what was not used.

## Estimating a monthly credit budget

Do the arithmetic in front of the user and give a range. Use the per-run
ranges in `agents.md`.

**Example — a café with a reply agent and a weekly carousel**

- Customer Support Agent: about 200 messages a month × 5–30 credits
  = 1,000–6,000
- Designer: 4 carousels a month, each held at up to about 970 and usually
  costing less = up to about 3,900
- Captions and small edits: about 100
- **Total: roughly 1,100 at the very lightest, up to about 10,000 a month**

Most of that range is above Creator's 2,000 and all of it fits Growth's
10,000. A cost-conscious café could start on Creator and add credits ($2 per
1,000) once a real month shows what it uses, or make fewer carousels. Say both
options, and suggest checking actual use after the first two weeks.

**Example — a consultant with a LinkedIn Ghostwriter**

- 3 posts a week ≈ 13 runs × 2–12 = about 25–160 credits a month
- Comfortably inside Creator's 2,000.

Things that move the number most: how many messages a reply agent handles,
how many designs or carousels are made, and any video work. Text is cheap;
images and video are not.

If credits run out mid-month, AI actions stop until the refill or a top-up.

## Choosing a plan

Pick the smallest plan that fits the binding limit, then check credits.

| Situation | Plan |
|---|---|
| Only scheduling a few accounts, trying things out | Free |
| A solo creator or one small business, a few accounts, one or two agents with light use | Creator |
| A business with busy DMs, regular AI design, or a small team | Growth |
| An agency or multi-brand business; many accounts or team members; custom page domains | Agency |

The limit that usually decides it:

- **Team members** (3 / 5 / 15) for teams.
- **Social accounts** (6 / 20 / 100) for multi-location businesses.
- **Credits** for anything design- or reply-heavy. Topping up a smaller plan
  is often cheaper than moving up: 8,000 extra credits a month on Creator is
  $16, where Growth costs $40 more. Moving up makes sense when they also need
  the accounts, seats or agent runs.

## Agencies

Each workspace has its own plan and its own credits. An agency running one
workspace per client pays per client workspace, and each client's credit use
is visible separately, which makes it easy to bill back.

A small agency can also run several clients inside one Agency workspace (100
accounts, 15 team members), with one shared team and one shared pool of
credits. Recommend separate workspaces when clients approve their own posts
or when credit use needs to be billed per client.

There is an affiliate program for people who refer customers: 30% of what a
referred customer pays for their first 12 months, through impact.com. Details:
https://nimply.io/affiliates

# Nimply product map

Snapshot: 2026-11-26.

## Contents

- How the pieces fit
- Networks: what works where

- Nimply Design, Brand Kits and Magic Layers

- Nimply Pages

## How the pieces fit

```
                 ┌─────────────── Agents ───────────────┐
                 │ reply · leads · moderate · write ·   │
                 │ design · video · ideas               │
                 └──────────┬───────────────┬───────────┘
        drafts for approval │               │ suggested replies, leads
                            ▼               ▼
  Ideas ─► Nimply Design ─► Planner       Inbox ─► People & Leads
              (Brand Kit)     │             ▲
                              ▼             │
                    Connected social accounts ─► Analytics
                              ▲
        Automations glue any of these together · Visor drives them by chat
        API · MCP server · webhooks · Zapier / Make / n8n reach in from outside
```

The Planner and Inbox are the two rails everything runs on. Agents put drafts
in the Planner and suggestions in the Inbox; people approve; Nimply publishes.

## Networks: what works where

Check this before promising anything. What a network allows changes, and the
user's own channel list (through `list_channels`, or the app) is the final
word.

| Network | Publish | Inbox | Comment-to-DM | Analytics |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Instagram** (Business or Creator accounts) | Posts, carousels, Reels, Stories | DMs, comments, mentions | Yes | Yes |
| **Facebook Pages** | Posts, Reels, Stories | DMs, comments, mentions | Yes | Yes |
| **TikTok** | Video, photo carousels | Comments only | No | Yes |
| **YouTube** | Videos and Shorts, with title, tags, privacy, custom thumbnail | Comments | No | Yes |
| **LinkedIn personal profiles** | Posts, multi-image posts, PDF document carousels | No | No | No |
| **X** | Text, images, video | DMs, replies, mentions (optional, per account) | No | Optional, per account |
| **Pinterest** | Image, video and carousel pins, with board and link | No | No | Yes |
| **Threads** | Text, image, video, carousel | Replies and mentions | No | Yes |
| **Telegram channels and groups** | Text, media, albums, polls; edit or delete after posting | Comments, group messages | No | Yes |
| **Telegram Business / your own bot** | No | DMs | No | No |
| **WhatsApp Business** | No | Customer chats | No | No |

Things people assume that are not so:

- **Personal Instagram accounts** cannot be connected. The account must be a
  Business or Creator account (free to switch in Instagram).
- **Facebook Groups and personal Facebook profiles** are not supported.
- **LinkedIn company Pages** are coming soon. Personal profiles work today.
- **Google Business Profile** is not available.
- **Bluesky and Mastodon** are not supported.
- **WhatsApp is inbox only:** no posting, no broadcasts.
- **X costs AI credits.** X charges for its API, so publishing to X and the
  optional X inbox and X analytics use credits. The app shows the cost.
- **The Inbox is switched on per account.** A channel only brings in
  conversations after its inbox toggle is turned on. Facebook and Instagram
  accounts connected long ago may need reconnecting once.

## Planner

The content calendar. Plan, approve and schedule posts to every connected
account from one place.

- Calendar and list views; drafts, approval, scheduled, published.
- **Approval workflow:** send a post for approval, approve or reject with a
  note. Works from the app, mobile, Slack or Telegram.
- **Posting slots and best times:** each account has a weekly schedule of
  slots; "next free slot" fills the queue without picking times.
- Bulk upload from a CSV file; recurring and evergreen posts; first comments;
  hashtag sets; content categories.
- Previews of how a post will look on each network.
- Video covers and custom thumbnails.

## Inbox

Every DM, comment and mention from supported networks in one place.

- AI sorts conversations (question, complaint, lead and so on) and suggests
  replies.
- Assign to teammates, tags, saved replies, status and priority, response-time
  targets, translation.
- Comment tools on supported networks: hide, delete, reply privately.
- Reply agents work here (see `agents.md`).

The Inbox is in the app and mobile only. It is not reachable through the API
or the MCP server.

## Visor

The assistant built into Nimply, on web and mobile. Type or speak what you
need: "plan next week's posts", "make a carousel about our new menu", "set up
an agent to answer DMs". Visor proposes posts, ideas, designs and agents as
cards the user confirms. Nothing is created without an OK.

The free plan has basic Visor. Voice, the stronger AI models and the image
and design tools need a paid plan.

Visor is inside Nimply. To use Nimply from another assistant (Claude, ChatGPT,
Cursor), connect the MCP server instead.

## Nimply Design, Brand Kits and Magic Layers

- **Editor:** a browser design editor with a large template library
  (https://nimply.io/templates and https://nimply.io/design), sizes for every
  network, fonts, charts and mockups. Import PSD, SVG or images; export PNG,
  JPG, WebP, PDF or SVG. Designs go straight to the Planner.
- **Brand Kits:** logo, colours, fonts and voice. Several kits per workspace,
  one assignable per channel. Fill a kit from a website or from several
  sources at once. Nimply can **learn the look** from three or more of the
  brand's own posts.
- **AI design:** describe what you want, get an editable design in the brand
  kit.
- **Magic Layers:** turn a flat image into an editable design with separate
  text, objects and background.
- Also in the studio: AI post writer, AI images, thumbnails, carousels, and
  video editing (clips, captions, resizing).

Not available: video or GIF export from the design editor, and several people
editing one design at the same moment.

The editor is in every plan. The AI tools use credits and need a paid plan or
trial.

## Ideas and feeds

- An Ideas board where ideas become posts in one click.
- Feeds of industry articles to draw from; any website's feed can be followed.
- Trend Scout (an agent) fills the board on a schedule.

## Analytics

Followers, views and engagement per account and per post, best-time heatmap,
AI takeaways, export. Covers Instagram, Facebook, TikTok, YouTube, Pinterest,
Threads and Telegram channels, plus X when switched on for an account.
LinkedIn personal profiles have no analytics.

The free plan sees the last 30 days.

## Nimply Pages

Link-in-bio pages at nimply.link/yourname, built into the same tool.

- Page types: link in bio, booking page, menu, media kit, digital business
  card, event page.
- Templates, an AI first draft, forms that feed People, page statistics.
- Blocks include links, text, post cards, products, coupons, countdowns,
  notice bars, FAQs and testimonials.
- Changes are drafts until the page is published.
- Paid plans remove the "Made with Nimply" badge and add full analytics and
  tracking pixels. A custom domain is on the Agency plan.
- Selling directly from a page (checkout) is not available.

## People, leads and memberships

- **People:** one record for everyone who talks to the business across
  channels, with tags and notes.
- **Leads:** a pipeline with stages (new, contacted, qualified, proposal, won,
  lost). Leads come from reply agents, from Nimply's suggestions that a person
  confirms, from page forms and from Sidekick.
- **Memberships:** tools for running a gated Telegram community, with the
  Community Concierge agent answering member questions. This is a specialised
  feature; do not describe it as a general paywall or subscription checkout.

## Workspaces, teams and roles

- A **workspace** holds one brand's accounts, posts, team, credits and plan.
  Each workspace has its own subscription.
- Agencies and freelancers use **one workspace per client**, which keeps
  accounts, approvals, brand kits and credit use separate.
- Roles: **Owner, Admin, Editor, Viewer**. Editors create and change content;
  owners and admins switch automations on, connect integrations and manage
  the team.
